question: Explain the provisions relating to filing and disposal of an appeal before the Appellate Authority under section 107 of the CGST Act, 2017.

points.label: Who may appeal and time limit
points.description: Any person aggrieved by an order of an adjudicating authority may appeal within three months of the order being communicated; the department may appeal after review by the Commissioner within six months; the Appellate Authority may allow one further month for sufficient cause.

points.label: Pre-deposit
points.description: An appeal can be filed only after paying in full the tax, interest, fine, fee and penalty admitted by the appellant, plus a sum equal to 10% of the remaining tax in dispute, subject to the maximum amount set in the section.

points.label: Stay of recovery
points.description: Once the pre-deposit is paid, recovery of the balance amount is deemed to be stayed until the appeal is disposed of.

points.label: Hearing and powers
points.description: The appellant is given an opportunity of being heard, with no more than three adjournments; the Authority may make further inquiry and confirm, modify or annul the order, but cannot send the case back to the adjudicating authority. Before enhancing a penalty or fine, reducing a refund or credit, or confirming tax not demanded, it must issue a show cause notice.

points.label: Order and further appeal
points.description: The order is in writing and states the points for decision, the decision and the reasons; where possible the appeal is decided within one year of filing. A person aggrieved may appeal further to the Appellate Tribunal.
points.basis: CGST Act, 2017, section 107(12) and (13), and section 112
